key_insight: In photonic hybrid quantum neural networks, hardware noise can sometimes serve as a built-in regularizer, but its benefit depends strongly on the dataset and noise configuration.
engineering_relevance: This suggests quantum hardware noise does not always need to be fully suppressed and may be exploitable during training to improve model generalization in some photonic quantum machine learning pipelines.
method: Built PHQCNNs in Quandela Perceval with the MerLin framework for Iris, Digits, and MNIST.
Injected Perceval’s 7-parameter physical noise model directly into training.
Used a genetic algorithm to search noise settings and compared them against a noiseless baseline across five random seeds.
evidence_signal: GA-tuned noise improved validation accuracy slightly on Iris (+0.82 pp) and Digits (+1.45 pp), but reduced performance on MNIST (-1.21 pp).
watch_item: No single noise parameter was consistently helpful, so the regularization effect is dataset-specific and requires careful joint tuning rather than assuming noise is universally beneficial.
paper_title: PN-QNN: Harnessing Physical Noise as a Native Regularizer in Photonic Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks
